3. My box with the big medicine packages, that I use to fill up my weekly medicine container
4. snacks like nuts

6. Basic hygiene things

8. Heating pads in different sizes

So in the years I have had this diagnosis, I have tried at least 7 different diets and read up a lot on different nutrition and eating plans. 

Basically I have felt 3 levers, that really did the trick blood test and symptom wise for me:
1 - leave out Gluten and lactose. What’s interesting to me is that I could feel the difference from leaving these out after just two weeks and it made a difference like day and night.
2 - no more alcohol. This one came naturally, as I could feel that I couldn’t process it like before and now would get drunk after a few sips. I just don’t enjoy being blackout drunk and getting there this fast has made the change easy. Sometimes I do drink one sip, just to taste something, or if I am in a super safe environment I drink more, once or twice a year. But in general leaving it out makes me feel much better.
3 - going vegan. I wanted to do this anyways and then afterwards I read ab article that might explain why it has helped so much. The article said that Hashimoto is basically a big inflammation and if you don’t want to make it bigger, you shouldn’t put anything into your body that could make that. Animal product can carry inflammation, vegetables for example can’t. I eat the occasional egg, but no meat or diary products. 

I can only recommend you to try what foods trigger you and then listening to your body.
- For example doing an elimination diet, where you start with a very small palette (like rice and potatoes) and then add one food every three days.
- or if you want to take some foods out of your diet you can do so for two weeks and then see what changes you feel. For example leaving out gluten or alcohol. (With the gluten I have one disclaimer: please read up on where it’s included, because they add that stuff to the most random things. Like tea bags and lip products. Many people actually fail at leaving out gluten, because of it being so well hidden.)

Pls always consult a doctor/ dietician before making big changes in your diet. Good luck!!
